desk.why: Implied is 1.10x the forecast realised vol and no event that has measurably moved NIFTY falls before expiry. A reason to buy is present (realised vol rising above implied, dealers short gamma) but buying on it has not paid on this desk's history.

facts: NIFTY moved +10.3% over the last 7 sessions and +1.1% on the day, to 25,301.
Gap +293 pts, then the session added -23 pts.
The day closed in the lower half (close - low 51, high - close 110).
ATM IV sits in its 88th percentile of the past year: option premium is rich - selling it pays more, but moves are expected to be bigger.

base.why: History says moves like this usually carry on (it reached 25,400 in 78.7% of past cases vs 64.3% normally), so the plan sells puts at 24,800, under the writers' floor at 25,200 and sells no call below 25,500.
text: bull put spread: sell 24,800 PE, buy 24,600 PE (credit about 26 pts, Rs 1,667 per lot; max loss Rs 11,333)

watch: Two daily closes below 25,400 without a new high
Close - open (the body) small, either colour
scenarios.means: The move is pausing. Time decay is working for the seller.
scenarios.action: Hold. Add a bear call spread: sell 25,500 CE, buy 25,700 CE (credit about 60 pts, Rs 3,925 per lot; max loss Rs 9,075) to turn it into an iron condor.

scenarios.title: Reaches 25,400 and stalls
watch: High - close bigger than close - low (sellers took it back)
25,400 CE open interest still rising (call writers defending)
scenarios.means: Call writers are defending 25,400. A ceiling for now.
scenarios.action: Close today's position (take the profit) and open the new one. It would be about Rs 1,347 in profit per lot here (estimated). Weekly: sell an iron condor, sell 25,400 CE / buy 25,600 CE / sell 25,100 PE / buy 24,900 PE. Call writers are defending 25,400: sell calls at the wall and keep a put spread under the market, so both sides earn while it stalls.

scenarios.title: Breaks out above 25,400
watch: 25,400 CE open interest falling (writers buying back - short covering)
Close near the day's high again
scenarios.means: The ceiling gave way. Next magnets: 25,500 then 25,800.
scenarios.action: Close today's position (take the profit) and open the new one. It would be about Rs 1,433 in profit per lot here (estimated). Weekly: sell a spread, sell 25,400 PE / buy 25,200 PE. The old ceiling 25,400 becomes the floor: sell puts at it. No calls below 25,800. Or buy a spread: buy 25,400 CE / sell 25,800 CE. If it spikes past 25,500 in one session with VIX rising, take profit instead of chasing.
scenarios.odds: Reached 25,500 in 68.1% and 25,800 in 34.0% of past cases (normal 51.2% / 22.5%).

scenarios.title: Pulls back to 25,200
watch: Holds: daily close above 25,200 and 25,200 PE open interest still rising
Breaks: daily close below 25,200 and 25,200 PE open interest falling
scenarios.means: A test of the put writers' floor. Shakeouts are normal after strong runs.
scenarios.action: If it holds: keep today's position, or add nothing (weekly). If it breaks: close today's position and switch to sell 25,200 CE / buy 25,400 CE (weekly). Exact strikes for every expiry are in the position matrix.
scenarios.odds: Dipped to 25,200 at some point in 55.3% of past cases (normal 55.4%).

rules: Take profit on any spread once 50% of its credit is earned; the rest is not worth the risk.
Close any spread once its loss reaches 1.5x the credit taken, whatever day that is. Holding into expiry is fine; size smaller on expiry day.
Act on daily closes, not intraday spikes. The OI checks use the next morning's bhavcopy.
Credits for rolls and add-ons are set by prices on the day you act; today's numbers are a guide only.
limits: None of the desk's positioning signals (PCR, max pain, OI flow, walls) has passed its own backtest for this horizon, so the history study is the main evidence.
